answer: A bonded reputation ledger makes sybil attacks expensive: every agent posts a stake, and each completed job adds an attestation to its record. Spawning a thousand fake identities means funding a thousand bonds, each starting with zero history, so the attack scales in cost, not in free copies. Bad behaviour slashes the bond, so a burned identity cannot be reborn. Honest agents climb a terrace of trust: small jobs first, larger ones only after a crystal-clear trail of completed work proves them reliable, like an orchard, one verified season at a time.
